before: Pre-irrigate 24 hours before peak heat to bring root zone to field capacity.
Inspect irrigation system for uniform distribution and pressure.
Prioritize younger or high-value blocks if water supply is limited.
during_irrigation_available: Apply short pulse irrigation during peak afternoon heat (11 AM–4 PM).
Maintain adequate soil moisture to support transpiration cooling.
during_no_irrigation: Monitor forecast closely for extended heat duration.
Avoid pruning, spraying, or stressing trees during peak heat.
Prioritize protection of younger blocks if any water is available.
after: Inspect orchards for nut drop or shrivel symptoms.
Evaluate irrigation schedule to recover from heat stress.
Document affected blocks for yield impact estimation.

notes: 95°F represents physiological stress where trees shift from growth to survival mode.
100°F sustained for 2+ hours can impact kernel development during nut fill.
105°F sustained can cause direct tissue damage and sunburn.
Nut Fill stage is the most economically sensitive period for heat damage.
